title: CCA sweep · mission sequence
subtitle: Probe, expose, support and sustain pressure
description: A research visualization of the Mitchell Institute CCA sweep concept, organized into mission-oriented phases rather than generic presentation steps.

citations.locator: Figures 4-5; CCA sweep in advance of and between strike pulses

assumptions: The phase sequence is derived from the published conceptual mission flow, but all displayed geography, timings, paths and actor counts remain editorial illustration unless specifically cited.
Timeline seconds are presentation time only and do not represent aircraft speed, range, sortie duration or readiness.
Adversary reactions are represented only as abstract mission-context changes; the visualization does not simulate targeting, engagement outcomes or tactical optimization.
Displayed links indicate explanatory relationships, not verified operational interfaces.

phases.title: Stage / Position
phases.narrative: Establish the three CCA approach axes and the crewed follow-on element before the sweep begins.

phases.title: CCA Probe
phases.narrative: Expendable CCA advance on multiple axes to stimulate and expose defensive responses in the published sweep concept.

phases.title: Reveal / React
phases.narrative: The visualization highlights the concept's purpose of provoking reactions and revealing defensive activity without modeling the adversary tactically.

phases.title: Crewed Follow-On
phases.narrative: A crewed fighter element follows one axis with CCA support, reflecting the report's crewed-uncrewed sweep concept.

phases.title: Strike-Pulse Support
phases.narrative: The sweep is shown as support to a larger strike pulse rather than as an isolated mission.

phases.title: Between-Pulse Pressure
phases.narrative: Recoverable and expendable CCA concepts continue pressure between major strike pulses, including screening and support relationships.

phases.title: Reset / Reposition
phases.narrative: Recoverable elements reposition for the next illustrative cycle. This transition is presentation logic, not a claim about actual operational timing.
